request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The rollover now also soft-closes every period of the old fiscal year that is still open, in
start-date order, each as a soft close would (PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED), after the ROLLOVER line.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A rollover now also soft-closes every period of the old fiscal year that is still open. I ran `bin/e2e` and all 4 acceptance tests pass.

The change is one line at the end of `rollover` in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/period/PeriodService.java`, plus an update to its doc comment:

```java
old.stream().filter(p -> !p.isFixed()).forEach(p -> fix(sheetId, user, p, false, true));
```

- **Which periods:** only the old year's periods that are neither closed nor soft-closed. In the test, 2026-11 was already closed, so it stays closed and gets no new audit line.
- **How:** each one goes through the same internal step a manual soft close uses. That fixes its figures and writes a `PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED ... period=<name> total=<amount>` line to the audit file.
- **Order:** start-date order, because the old periods are already read sorted by from-date. These lines come after the `ROLLOVER` line, as the request asks.

It skips the role check a manual soft close does. Only a steward can roll the year over, and that is already checked first.

Undoing a rollover still removes only the new year's periods. The old-year periods it soft-closed stay soft-closed after an undo.

No database or front-end changes were needed.
